FACT.Influenza: Flu mutates fast. Last year's antibodies may not fit.
FACT.COVID-19: Can inflame the heart muscle (myocarditis) as well as the lungs.
FACT.RSV: Mild in adults, dangerous for babies.
FACT.Chickenpox: Hides in nerves for decades. Returns as shingles.
FACT.Glandular fever: Hides inside your own B-cells; risks spleen rupture.
FACT.Tuberculosis: Can lie dormant in the lungs for years.
FACT.Whooping cough: Violent coughing fits; DPT vaccine prevents it.
FACT.Chikungunya: Mosquito virus; joint pain, sometimes myocarditis.
FACT.Yellow fever: Attacks the liver. Hence the jaundice.
FACT.Rabies: Creeps inside nerves where antibodies can't follow.
FACT.Lyme disease: Tick bite; can cause Lyme carditis in the heart.
FACT.Plague: Flea bites. The historical Black Death.
FACT.MRSA: A superbug. In the blood it can seed ANY organ, including heart valves.
FACT.Cellulitis: Staph/Strep skin infection; can settle on heart valves.
FACT.Leptospirosis: Enters through cuts in floodwater. A monsoon risk.
FACT.Gas gangrene: Destroys deep tissue fast; a surgical emergency.
FACT.Cold sore: Retreats into nerves to hide from antibodies.
FACT.Typhoid: Unclean water; hits liver and spleen.
FACT.Food poisoning: Some E. coli damage the kidneys (HUS).
FACT.Rotavirus: A top cause of child diarrhoea. Vaccine-preventable.
FACT.Hepatitis A: A liver virus from contaminated food or water.
FACT.Polio: Enters via the gut, attacks nerves.

Influenza.d: Virus isolated 1933; the 1918 pandemic killed ~50 million.
Influenza.c: Fever, aches, cough; can lead to pneumonia and myocarditis.
Influenza.p: Annual flu vaccine. It changes because the virus mutates fast.
Influenza.r: Rest, fluids; antivirals for high-risk patients.

Common cold.r: No cure; it passes in about a week.

COVID-19.d: SARS-CoV-2 identified in Wuhan, China, December 2019.
COVID-19.c: Cough, fever, loss of smell; pneumonia and myocarditis in severe cases.
COVID-19.r: Supportive care; antivirals for those at risk.

RSV.c: Cold-like illness; bronchiolitis and pneumonia in babies.
RSV.p: Monoclonal antibodies and a maternal vaccine for infants.

Measles.d: Vaccine by John Enders, 1963. One of the most contagious viruses known.
Measles.c: Rash and fever. And IMMUNE AMNESIA: it wipes out your existing immune memory, leaving you open to diseases you had already beaten.
Measles.r: No antiviral; vitamin A and supportive care. Prevention is everything.

Mumps.c: Swollen salivary glands; can inflame the brain and testes.

Rubella.d: Link to birth defects found by Norman Gregg, 1941.
Rubella.c: Mild rash in children. But devastating to an unborn baby.
Rubella.r: No cure; prevention protects the next generation.

Smallpox.d: Jenner's cowpox vaccine, 1796. The first vaccine ever made.
Smallpox.c: Disfiguring pustules; killed around 30% of those infected.
Smallpox.w: NOWHERE. Declared eradicated in 1980. The only human disease ever wiped out.
Smallpox.p: Vaccination. The campaign that ended it.
Smallpox.r: None needed. This card is a trophy: proof that immunology WINS.

Nipah.d: Identified in Malaysia 1998; outbreaks in Kerala, India (2018, 2023).
Nipah.c: Brain inflammation; fatal in 40-75% of cases.
Nipah.w: South and Southeast Asia; spread by fruit bats.
Nipah.p: Avoid raw date-palm sap; isolate cases.

Hand-foot-and-mouth.c: Blisters on hands, feet and mouth; usually mild in children.

Chickenpox.c: Itchy blisters. Then HIDES IN YOUR NERVES for decades and can return as shingles.

Glandular fever.c: Fever, sore throat, extreme fatigue, swollen spleen (rupture risk).
Glandular fever.r: Rest. Avoid contact sport while the spleen is swollen.

Cytomegalovirus.c: Harmless in healthy people. It just hides for life. Dangerous to babies and the immunosuppressed.

Tuberculosis.c: Chronic cough, weight loss, night sweats. Can lie dormant for YEARS.
Tuberculosis.w: Worldwide. India carries the largest burden of any country.
Tuberculosis.p: BCG vaccine; treating active cases; ventilation.
Tuberculosis.r: 6+ months of combination antibiotics. Not finishing the course breeds resistance.

Whooping cough.c: Violent coughing fits with a 'whoop'; deadly in babies.

Meningitis.c: Infects the lining of the brain. Can kill a healthy person within HOURS.

Pneumonia.c: Fills the lungs with fluid. The single biggest infectious killer of children worldwide.
Pneumonia.p: Pneumococcal vaccine; flu vaccine; clean cooking fuel.

Strep throat.c: Sore throat. But if ignored, the antibodies you make against it can attack YOUR OWN HEART VALVES (rheumatic fever).
Strep throat.w: Worldwide; rheumatic heart disease is a major problem in India.
Strep throat.r: Antibiotics. Which are given mainly to prevent the heart damage.

Leprosy.d: Bacterium found by Gerhard Hansen, 1873. The first bacterium ever linked to human disease.
Leprosy.c: Attacks the nerves. Numbness means injuries go unnoticed, and THAT causes the deformity. Not the germ eating the flesh, as people wrongly believe.
Leprosy.w: India records a large share of the world's new cases.
Leprosy.p: IT IS NOT SPREAD BY TOUCH. It spreads by droplets, after months of close contact, and about 95% of people are naturally immune to it. It enters through the NOSE, which is why it is in the Nose lane and not the Contact lane. The belief that a handshake spreads leprosy is a myth that exiled people to colonies for centuries.
Leprosy.r: Completely curable with multi-drug therapy. Free worldwide since 1995.

Legionnaires' disease.d: Named after a 1976 outbreak at an American Legion convention.
Legionnaires' disease.c: Severe pneumonia from bacteria in air-conditioning and water systems.
Legionnaires' disease.w: Worldwide, in buildings with poorly maintained water systems.
Legionnaires' disease.p: Maintain cooling towers and water tanks.

Diphtheria.d: Antitoxin by von Behring, 1890. Winning the FIRST Nobel Prize in Medicine.
Diphtheria.c: A grey membrane chokes the throat, and its TOXIN attacks the heart. The toxin is pre-formed. It poisons you directly.
Diphtheria.w: Worldwide where vaccination lapses; outbreaks still occur in India.
Diphtheria.r: ANTITOXIN. Antibodies. No cell can eat a toxin.

Mucormycosis.d: 'Black fungus'. Surged across India in 2021 among COVID patients.
Mucormycosis.c: Invades nose and sinuses, then the eye and BRAIN. Often fatal.
Mucormycosis.w: Worldwide, but it strikes the immunocompromised. Diabetics, steroid patients.
Mucormycosis.r: Antifungals and surgery. A pure OPPORTUNIST. It only wins when your defences are already down.

Aspergillosis.c: A mould you breathe in daily. Harmless, unless your defences are weak.
Aspergillosis.r: Antifungals. Neutrophils are the key defence. Which is why neutropenia invites it in.

Cryptococcus.d: Described 1894; a leading killer in AIDS.
Cryptococcus.c: Fungal meningitis. It invades the BRAIN.
Cryptococcus.w: Worldwide, in soil and pigeon droppings.
Cryptococcus.p: Hard to avoid; the real defence is a working immune system.
Cryptococcus.r: Antifungals. Mostly attacks people with HIV.

Pneumocystis pneumonia.d: Recognised in the 1980s as the disease that revealed AIDS.
Pneumocystis pneumonia.c: A fungus that only causes pneumonia when helper T-cells are destroyed.
Pneumocystis pneumonia.r: Antibiotics/antifungals. It is a signpost of a collapsed immune system.

Dengue.d: Four different serotypes. This matters enormously.
Dengue.c: High fever, severe joint pain, crashing platelets (marrow).
Dengue.w: Tropics; a major monsoon disease across India.
Dengue.p: Aedes mosquito control. It bites in DAYTIME. Remove standing water.
Dengue.r: No cure; fluids. Never give aspirin. A SECOND dengue infection can be far worse (ADE).

Chikungunya.d: First described in Tanzania, 1952. The name means 'to become contorted'.
Chikungunya.c: Fever and severe joint pain that can last months.
Chikungunya.w: Africa, Asia, the Americas; common in India.

Japanese encephalitis.c: Brain inflammation; often leaves permanent damage.
Japanese encephalitis.w: Rural Asia including India; pigs and birds are the reservoir.

Yellow fever.d: Shown to be mosquito-borne by Walter Reed, 1900.
Yellow fever.c: Fever, liver failure and jaundice (the 'yellow'), bleeding.

Zika.d: Identified 1947; caused a global emergency in 2015-16.
Zika.c: Mild in adults. But causes severe brain defects in unborn babies.

West Nile fever.c: Usually mild; occasionally causes brain inflammation.

Rabies.c: Creeps up your NERVES to the brain, where antibodies cannot follow. Almost 100% fatal once symptoms begin.
Rabies.w: Worldwide; dogs are the main source in India.
Rabies.p: Vaccinate dogs. After a bite: wash it, and get the vaccine IMMEDIATELY.
Rabies.r: Post-exposure vaccine works BEFORE symptoms start. After that, nothing does.

HIV.d: Identified 1983 by Montagnier and Barré-Sinoussi (Nobel Prize).
HIV.c: It destroys HELPER T-CELLS. The commanders of your immune system. Without them, ordinary germs become lethal.
HIV.w: Worldwide; ~39 million people live with HIV. Spread by unprotected sex, shared needles, and infected blood.
HIV.p: Condoms; never share needles; screened blood; PrEP medication. It is NOT spread by mosquitoes, sharing food, or touching. A myth worth killing.
HIV.r: Antiretroviral therapy: not a cure, but people now live full lives, and treatment makes them unable to pass it on. Attacking the immune system itself is why HIV is so dangerous.

Hepatitis B.d: Discovered by Baruch Blumberg, 1965 (Nobel Prize). First anti-cancer vaccine.
Hepatitis B.c: Attacks the liver; can persist for life and cause liver cancer.
Hepatitis B.p: Hepatitis B vaccine. Given at birth in India.
Hepatitis B.r: Antivirals control it; the vaccine prevents it.

Hepatitis C.c: Silently scars the liver for decades. Cirrhosis and cancer.
Hepatitis C.p: No vaccine yet; screened blood and clean needles.
Hepatitis C.r: CURABLE since 2014 with direct-acting antivirals. One of medicine's great wins.

Chagas disease.d: Discovered by Carlos Chagas, 1909. He found the parasite, the vector and the disease.
Chagas disease.c: A parasite that HIDES INSIDE HEART MUSCLE for decades, then destroys it.
Chagas disease.r: Drugs work early; once the heart is damaged, it is irreversible.

Lyme disease.c: Bull's-eye rash; can attack the heart (Lyme carditis) and nerves.
Lyme disease.w: North America, Europe, parts of Asia. From tick bites.
Lyme disease.p: Cover skin in woods; remove ticks quickly.
Lyme disease.r: Antibiotics. Very effective if caught early.

Plague.d: Yersinia pestis. The Black Death killed a third of Europe (1347-51).
Plague.c: Swollen lymph nodes ('buboes'); the lung form spreads person to person and kills fast.
Plague.w: Rare now; pockets in Africa, Asia, the Americas.

Scrub typhus.d: Recognised in Asia; a major cause of fever in India.
Scrub typhus.c: Fever with a black scab at the mite bite; can cause pneumonia and brain inflammation.

Malaria.d: Ronald Ross proved mosquitoes carry it. In Secunderabad, INDIA, 1897. Nobel Prize.
Malaria.c: Bite → LIVER (hides inside liver cells) → bursts into blood → fever cycles, anaemia, cerebral malaria.
Malaria.w: Tropics; still a major disease in India.
Malaria.r: Antimalarials. P. vivax needs a SECOND drug to clear the liver. Or it relapses months later.

Malaria (blood).d: The blood stage. Merozoites bursting out of the liver.
Malaria (blood).c: Invades red blood cells; causes the classic fever cycles.
Malaria (blood).r: NOW antibodies and phagocytes can reach it. This is the stage you can actually fight.

Kala-azar.d: Visceral leishmaniasis. Sir Upendranath Brahmachari developed the first cure. In India, 1920.
Kala-azar.c: HIDES INSIDE YOUR MACROPHAGES. It turns your own defender cell into its home. Destroys the spleen; fatal untreated.
Kala-azar.w: Bihar, India, has historically carried a large share of the world's cases.
Kala-azar.r: Liposomal amphotericin B. India has driven cases down dramatically.

Sleeping sickness.d: African trypanosomiasis; the parasite was found in 1901.
Sleeping sickness.c: ANTIGENIC VARIATION. It keeps changing its coat, so your antibodies never quite fit. Eventually invades the brain.
Sleeping sickness.w: Sub-Saharan Africa; spread by the tsetse fly.
Sleeping sickness.r: Drugs exist, and cases have collapsed. Its trick. Changing disguise. Is why a vaccine is so hard.

Filariasis.d: Elephantiasis; the worm was found by Patrick Manson, 1877.
Filariasis.c: Adult worms BLOCK YOUR LYMPHATIC VESSELS. Fluid cannot drain, and limbs swell enormously.
Filariasis.w: Tropics; India has run one of the world's largest elimination programmes.
Filariasis.r: Antiparasitic drugs kill the worms; the swelling is often permanent.

Snake venom.d: Antivenom invented by Albert Calmette, 1895. Using antibodies from horses.
Snake venom.c: Not alive, not a germ. A mix of toxic proteins. Attacks heart, kidneys and nerves.
Snake venom.w: India has the world's highest snakebite death toll. Roughly 58,000 a year.
Snake venom.p: Boots and a torch after dark; never reach blindly into grass.
Snake venom.r: ANTIVENOM. Borrowed antibodies. PASSIVE immunity: instant, but temporary.

Russell's viper venom.c: Destroys blood clotting and shreds the KIDNEYS. A leading cause of snakebite death in India.
Russell's viper venom.p: Boots; clear rubble near homes; torch at night.
Russell's viper venom.r: Antivenom, urgently. Dialysis may be needed for the kidneys.

Red scorpion sting.d: Indian red scorpion. Among the most lethal scorpions in the world.
Red scorpion sting.c: Venom floods the body with adrenaline; the HEART and LUNGS fail.
Red scorpion sting.w: Western and southern India; a major cause of child deaths in some districts.
Red scorpion sting.p: Shake out shoes; seal home floors.
Red scorpion sting.r: The drug prazosin transformed survival. An Indian medical breakthrough.

Tetanus.d: Toxin isolated 1890 by Kitasato and von Behring.
Tetanus.c: Its TOXIN locks the muscles rigid. 'lockjaw'. Not contagious at all.
Tetanus.p: Tetanus vaccine and boosters; clean wounds.
Tetanus.r: Antitoxin and intensive care. Only antibodies can neutralise a toxin.

MRSA.c: Skin abscesses. And in the blood it can seed ANY organ, including heart valves.
MRSA.r: Only a few antibiotics still work. The classic superbug.

Cellulitis.c: Hot, red, spreading skin infection; can reach blood, bone and heart valves.

Leptospirosis.c: Fever, then kidney and liver failure (Weil's disease).
Leptospirosis.w: Tropics; a monsoon and flood disease in India.
Leptospirosis.p: Avoid wading in floodwater with open cuts; rodent control.

Gas gangrene.d: Clostridium perfringens. Notorious in the trenches of WWI.
Gas gangrene.c: Destroys tissue fast, producing gas; its toxins poison the kidneys.
Gas gangrene.r: Surgery plus antibiotics. A true emergency.

Syphilis.d: Bacterium found 1905; the first 'magic bullet' drug (Salvarsan) targeted it.
Syphilis.c: Progresses over years to attack the brain and heart. Can pass to an unborn baby.
Syphilis.r: Penicillin. Still completely effective after 80 years.

Brucellosis.d: Traced to goat's milk by David Bruce, 1887.
Brucellosis.c: Undulating fever; settles in the spleen, liver and bones.
Brucellosis.w: Worldwide, from unpasteurised milk and infected livestock.

Cold sore.d: Herpes simplex virus; known since antiquity.
Cold sore.c: Blisters on the lip. Then retreats into your NERVES to hide from antibodies.
Cold sore.r: Antivirals shorten attacks. It is never fully cleared.

Human papillomavirus.d: Link to cervical cancer proven by Harald zur Hausen (Nobel Prize, 2008).
Human papillomavirus.c: Hides inside cells for years and can turn them cancerous. It causes almost ALL cervical cancer.
Human papillomavirus.w: Worldwide; most adults meet it at some point.
Human papillomavirus.p: The HPV VACCINE. The first vaccine that prevents a cancer. India began rolling it out nationally; it works best given before exposure.
Human papillomavirus.r: No antiviral. Screening catches early changes. This is the clearest case in the whole deck of a vaccine stopping a cancer before it starts.

Ebola.d: First outbreak near the Ebola River, 1976.
Ebola.c: Massive internal bleeding; liver and spleen collapse. Kills up to 90%.
Ebola.p: Isolation, protective equipment. And now a working vaccine.
Ebola.r: Antibody treatments and supportive care; survival has improved greatly.

Anthrax.d: Robert Koch used it in 1876 to PROVE germs cause disease. Pasteur vaccinated sheep in 1881.
Anthrax.c: Its TOXIN kills cells directly; the inhaled form is nearly always fatal.
Anthrax.r: Antibiotics plus ANTITOXIN. The toxin must be neutralised separately.

Hookworm.d: Linked to anaemia by Arthur Looss, 1898. He infected himself by accident.
Hookworm.c: Burrows in through BARE SKIN, travels to the gut, and drinks your blood. Causing anaemia.
Hookworm.w: Warm damp soil where people walk barefoot.

Schistosomiasis.c: Larvae penetrate skin in fresh water; adult worms scar the liver and bladder.
Schistosomiasis.w: Africa, Middle East, parts of Asia.
Schistosomiasis.p: Avoid infested fresh water; snail control.

Guinea worm.d: Ancient. Possibly the 'fiery serpent' of the Bible.
Guinea worm.c: A metre-long worm slowly emerges through the skin.
Guinea worm.w: ALMOST ERADICATED. From 3.5 million cases in 1986 to a handful today.
Guinea worm.p: Filter drinking water. No drug, no vaccine. Just clean water.
Guinea worm.r: Wind the worm out slowly. Proof that prevention alone can defeat a disease.

Histoplasmosis.c: A fungus from soil with bird or bat droppings; attacks the lungs and spleen.
Histoplasmosis.w: Worldwide, including river valleys of India.
Histoplasmosis.p: Avoid dusty caves and bird roosts.
Histoplasmosis.r: Antifungals; often self-limiting in healthy people.

Typhoid.d: Salmonella Typhi; 'Typhoid Mary' spread it while healthy herself.
Typhoid.c: Prolonged high fever; infects the liver, spleen and gut.
Typhoid.w: Where sanitation is poor. Common in South Asia.
Typhoid.r: Antibiotics. But drug-resistant typhoid is spreading in India and Pakistan.

Cholera.d: John Snow traced it to a London water pump in 1854. The birth of epidemiology.
Cholera.c: Its TOXIN forces the gut to pour out litres of water. Dehydration kills within hours.
Cholera.p: Clean water and sanitation; oral vaccine.
Cholera.r: Oral rehydration salts (ORS). Simple, cheap, and one of the great lifesavers.

Dysentery.c: Bloody diarrhoea; can damage the kidneys.

Food poisoning.d: E. coli described by Theodor Escherich, 1885.
Food poisoning.c: Cramps and diarrhoea; some strains harm the kidneys.

Listeria.c: Survives refrigeration; crosses into the BRAIN and the placenta.

Stomach ulcer (H. pylori).d: Barry Marshall DRANK the bacteria in 1984 to prove they cause ulcers. He won the Nobel Prize.
Stomach ulcer (H. pylori).c: Burrows into the stomach lining; causes ulcers and stomach cancer.
Stomach ulcer (H. pylori).w: Perhaps half the world carries it.
Stomach ulcer (H. pylori).r: Antibiotics CURE it. Ulcers were once thought to be caused by stress.

Rotavirus.c: Severe diarrhoea and dehydration in young children.
Rotavirus.w: Worldwide; a leading killer of children before vaccines.
Rotavirus.p: Rotavirus vaccine. Now in India's immunisation programme.

Hepatitis A.c: Liver inflammation and jaundice; no chronic form.

Hepatitis E.d: Recognised after outbreaks in INDIA in the 1970s-80s.
Hepatitis E.c: Liver inflammation; especially dangerous in pregnancy.

Norovirus.d: Traced to an outbreak in Norwalk, Ohio, 1968.
Norovirus.c: Sudden violent vomiting and diarrhoea; astonishingly contagious.
Norovirus.w: Worldwide. Famous on cruise ships and in schools.
Norovirus.r: Rehydration; passes in a couple of days.

Polio.c: Enters through the gut; destroys nerve cells and paralyses.
Polio.w: Nearly eradicated. INDIA was declared polio-free in 2014.
Polio.p: Oral polio vaccine. One of the great public-health triumphs.
Polio.r: No cure for the paralysis. Prevention is everything.

Botulism.d: Toxin identified 1895. The most poisonous substance known to science.
Botulism.c: Not alive. Paralyses every muscle, including breathing. A few nanograms can kill.
Botulism.p: Proper canning; never feed honey to infants.
Botulism.r: ANTITOXIN. (In tiny doses this same toxin is Botox.)

Shiga toxin (E. coli O157).c: Not alive. Destroys the KIDNEYS (haemolytic uraemic syndrome), especially in children.
Shiga toxin (E. coli O157).r: Supportive care and dialysis. Antibiotics can make it WORSE by releasing more toxin.

Roundworm.d: Ascaris lumbricoides. Grows up to 35 cm long.
Roundworm.c: Larvae migrate THROUGH THE LUNGS, then return to the gut. Can block the intestines.
Roundworm.w: Where sanitation is poor. One of the commonest infections on Earth.
Roundworm.r: Deworming tablets. Too big for any cell to swallow.

Tapeworm.d: Neurocysticercosis recognised as a major cause of epilepsy.
Tapeworm.c: Larvae form cysts IN THE BRAIN. A leading cause of adult-onset epilepsy in India.
Tapeworm.w: Where pigs are raised with poor sanitation.

Whipworm.c: Burrows into the gut wall; causes chronic blood loss and anaemia in children.

Amoebiasis.d: Entamoeba histolytica. The species name means 'tissue-dissolving'.
Amoebiasis.c: Eats through the gut wall and forms a LIVER ABSCESS.
Amoebiasis.w: Common in India and other tropical regions.
Amoebiasis.r: Metronidazole; the abscess may need draining.

Giardia.d: Seen by Antonie van Leeuwenhoek in 1681. In his own stool.
Giardia.c: Coats the gut and blocks absorption. You eat, but you starve. Draining your energy.
Giardia.w: Worldwide; 'beaver fever' from streams and unclean water.

Toxoplasmosis.c: Forms silent CYSTS IN THE BRAIN and hides there for life. Dangerous to unborn babies and to people with AIDS.
Toxoplasmosis.w: Worldwide. From undercooked meat and cat faeces.
Toxoplasmosis.p: Cook meat; pregnant women should avoid cat litter.

Candida.d: A yeast that lives on almost everyone, harmlessly.
Candida.c: Normally kept in check by your immune system and your other microbes. But if either falls, it invades ANY organ.
Candida.w: Everywhere. It is already on you right now.
Candida.p: Careful antibiotic use. Killing your good bacteria lets Candida bloom.

Scabies.d: The mite was seen under a microscope in 1687. Making scabies one of the FIRST diseases ever proven to have a specific cause.
Scabies.c: A mite that burrows into your skin and lays eggs. The unbearable itch is an ALLERGIC reaction to it. Your own immune system causing the misery.
Scabies.w: Worldwide; ~200 million people at any moment. Spreads by prolonged skin-to-skin contact and shared bedding.
Scabies.p: Treat the whole household at once, and wash all bedding.
Scabies.r: Permethrin cream or ivermectin. Cheap and curable. But it keeps coming back if only one person is treated.

Ringworm.d: Not a worm at all. A FUNGUS. The name comes from the ring-shaped rash.
Ringworm.c: A fungus digesting the keratin in your skin, hair and nails.
Ringworm.w: Everywhere. Spreads by touch, shared towels, and from animals.
Ringworm.p: Do not share towels or combs; keep skin dry.
Ringworm.r: Antifungal cream. The commonest fungal infection on Earth. And one of the most misnamed.

Impetigo.d: Streptococcus or Staphylococcus on the skin.
Impetigo.c: Golden crusted sores, mainly in children. Highly contagious by touch. Can lead to kidney damage.
Impetigo.w: Worldwide; common where it is hot and crowded.
Impetigo.p: Wash hands and cuts; do not share towels.

Trachoma.d: Chlamydia trachomatis. The SAME species that causes the sexually transmitted infection, arriving by a completely different route.
Trachoma.c: Repeated infection scars the eyelid until the lashes turn INWARD and scrape the eye. Blindness comes slowly, over years.
Trachoma.w: The world's leading INFECTIOUS cause of blindness. India has fought a long campaign against it.
Trachoma.p: Face-washing and clean water. The 'SAFE' strategy. Flies spread it between children's eyes.
Trachoma.r: A single dose of azithromycin. Surgery for the eyelid. **A disease of poverty, cured by soap and water.**

Conjunctivitis.c: Red, weeping, gritty eyes. Astonishingly contagious: rub your eye, touch a door handle, and the next person has it.
Conjunctivitis.p: Wash hands. Do not share towels or pillows.
Conjunctivitis.r: Usually clears itself. A NAKED virus. No envelope, so it survives on surfaces for days and hand-gel works poorly on it.

Molluscum contagiosum.d: A poxvirus. A distant cousin of smallpox.
Molluscum contagiosum.c: Small pearly bumps, spread by skin contact and shared towels. Harmless but stubborn.
Molluscum contagiosum.p: Do not share towels; cover the bumps.
Molluscum contagiosum.r: Usually clears on its own. But it can take a year. Your immune system gets there eventually.

Endocarditis.d: Infection of the heart valves. Described by William Osler, 1885.
Endocarditis.c: Bacteria in the bloodstream settle on a HEART VALVE and build a colony there, where blood flow shields them from your immune cells.
Endocarditis.w: Worldwide. A risk after dental work, IV drug use, or a contaminated line. And after rheumatic fever has damaged a valve.
Endocarditis.p: Treat bloodstream infections early; look after damaged valves.
Endocarditis.r: Weeks of intravenous antibiotics; sometimes surgery to replace the valve.

Gonorrhoea.c: Infects the reproductive tract; can spread to joints and heart valves. Often causes NO symptoms. So it spreads silently.
Gonorrhoea.w: Worldwide; about 82 million new cases a year.
Gonorrhoea.r: Antibiotics. But it has now defeated almost every antibiotic we have. The WHO lists it as a PRIORITY superbug. This is antibiotic resistance happening in real time.

Chlamydia.d: Chlamydia trachomatis. The same species that causes trachoma, the leading infectious cause of blindness.
Chlamydia.c: An INTRACELLULAR bacterium. It lives inside your cells, where antibodies struggle to reach. Usually silent; can cause infertility.
Chlamydia.w: The commonest bacterial STI in the world.
Chlamydia.r: Antibiotics. Easy to cure. But only if you know you have it.

Genital herpes.c: Like a cold sore, it retreats into your NERVES and hides there for life. Antibodies cannot follow it in.
Genital herpes.p: Condoms reduce but do not eliminate the risk.
Genital herpes.r: Antivirals control outbreaks. It is never cleared. A lifelong passenger.

Trichomoniasis.c: The commonest curable STI on Earth. Often silent.
Trichomoniasis.w: Worldwide. Around 156 million cases a year.
Trichomoniasis.r: A single course of metronidazole cures it.

Hepatitis D.d: Identified 1977. The strangest virus in this deck.
Hepatitis D.c: It is INCOMPLETE. It cannot infect you on its own: it can ONLY survive if Hepatitis B is already there, because it borrows Hep B's outer coat. A virus that parasitises another virus.
Hepatitis D.w: Wherever Hepatitis B is; the most severe form of viral hepatitis.
Hepatitis D.p: The Hepatitis B vaccine ALSO prevents Hepatitis D. Block the host and the passenger cannot land.
Hepatitis D.r: Hard to treat. Prevention through the Hep B vaccine is the real answer.

Transfusion malaria.d: Malaria delivered straight into the bloodstream by transfused blood.
Transfusion malaria.c: It SKIPS the mosquito and skips the tissues. It goes directly to the liver.
Transfusion malaria.w: Anywhere blood is not properly screened.
Transfusion malaria.p: Screening donated blood. Which is why blood banks test every unit.
Transfusion malaria.r: Antimalarials. This is why safe transfusion is a public-health issue, not just a hospital one.

Catheter sepsis.d: A fungal bloodstream infection from a drip line or catheter.
Catheter sepsis.c: Candida travelling up a plastic tube straight into your blood, bypassing every barrier you have.
Catheter sepsis.w: Hospitals worldwide. One of the commonest hospital-acquired infections.
Catheter sepsis.p: Sterile technique; remove lines as soon as they are not needed.
Catheter sepsis.r: Antifungals. A reminder that medicine itself can open a door.

Cannula infection.d: Bacteria entering through a drip needle.
Cannula infection.c: Staph from the skin, pushed straight into the bloodstream by a needle. Can seed the heart valves.
Cannula infection.p: Clean the skin; change the line; wash hands.

Tetanus toxin.c: Not alive. Locks the muscles rigid. It does not reproduce. It simply poisons.
Tetanus toxin.w: Released by tetanus bacteria in a wound.
Tetanus toxin.p: Tetanus vaccine trains you to make ANTITOXIN.
Tetanus toxin.r: Only antibodies can neutralise it. No cell can eat a toxin.

Cholera toxin.c: Not alive. Forces gut cells to pump out water; the kidneys fail from dehydration.

Clostridial toxin.c: Not alive. Destroys tissue and poisons the kidneys and liver.

Diphtheria toxin.d: The toxin von Behring made the first antitoxin against.
Diphtheria toxin.c: Not alive. Poisons the HEART muscle directly.

Shingles.c: The chickenpox virus hid in your nerves for decades and re-emerged.
Shingles.r: Antivirals. Proof that some viruses never truly leave.

Dengue (ADE).c: Your antibodies from a PREVIOUS dengue do not neutralise this serotype. They HELP it into your cells.
Dengue (ADE).p: Mosquito control. This is exactly why a dengue vaccine is so hard to make.
Dengue (ADE).r: Antibodies will NOT work here. Use cells.

Malaria (relapse).c: A dormant form of P. vivax slept in your liver and woke months later. From nothing.
Malaria (relapse).w: Wherever P. vivax occurs, including India.
Malaria (relapse).p: Finish the full course of primaquine to clear the liver.
Malaria (relapse).r: A second drug is needed specifically for the liver forms.

Tuberculosis (reactivated).d: Latency has been known since the 19th century.
Tuberculosis (reactivated).c: TB you thought you had beaten was only sleeping. It woke when your defences fell.
Tuberculosis (reactivated).w: About a quarter of the world carries latent TB.
Tuberculosis (reactivated).p: Treat latent TB in high-risk people.

Pneumococcal pneumonia.c: Moves into lungs stripped bare by influenza. This. Not the flu itself. Killed most victims in 1918.
